value: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the foundations of mathematics, beginning with fundamental concepts in mathematical logic, deduction systems, and type theory. It then extensively explores various approaches to set theory, encompassing material, structural, and class-set formulations, and details a wide array of foundational axioms, including those related to basic constructions, choice principles, and large cardinals. The article culminates with a focused discussion on classical logic, defining its key characteristics such as the principle of excluded middle, contrasting it with non-classical alternatives, and highlighting its role in underpinning classical mathematics.
